name: Fiona Mann
life: “I paid for my kitchen course making favors for weddings I never saw.” On Wednesday, near Ferris Deli, Fiona asks for the end slice and listens to the names the counter workers use for regulars.
voice: I can't eat the memorial sandwich. I chose the paper it will be wrapped in.
appearance: Fiona is easy to recognize by a cropped cut that shows the shape of the ears and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in an unlined tan jacket with a watch on a cracked leather band, Fiona counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices when listening.
personality: Fiona has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Fiona's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To choose paper that will carry the order without collapsing.
family: Rowan Davis is Fiona’s half-sibling. Fiona makes the call. Rowan is free to hang up first. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *School after sixty*, Rowan says, “I took the day off with a stomach ache. I don't want my boss at the bank to know I'm learning to read his notices.”
connections: Jules Drake. The remaining change and the wrapper give the anniversary order a price and a proper finish.

reactions.situation: The deli proposes serving the memorial sandwich every Sunday
reactions.response: Fiona asks the family what they would want to eat on an ordinary Sunday.

reactions.situation: An argument on the pavement makes a bystander feel unsafe
reactions.response: Fiona walks with the bystander to a staffed doorway and checks whether they want someone called.

reactions.response: Fiona seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Fiona seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
